summary: The note is a short biographical entry on Idries Shah, describing his birth in Simla, India, and his family background. It covers his Afghan-Indian father, Scottish mother, Musavi Sayyid paternal lineage, and the family's hereditary nawab title in Sardhana.
one_line: Biographical note on Idries Shah's birth in Simla and his Afghan-Indian and Scottish family background.
key_facts: Idries Shah was born in Simla, India.
Idries Shah's father was Sirdar Ikbal Ali Shah, a writer and diplomat.
Idries Shah's father was of Afghan-Indian background.
Idries Shah's mother was Saira Elizabeth Luiza Shah, who was Scottish.
The paternal side of Idries Shah's family were Musavi Sayyids.
The ancestral home of Idries Shah's paternal family was near the Paghman Gardens of Kabul.
Idries Shah's paternal grandfather was Sayed Amjad Ali Shah.
Sayed Amjad Ali Shah was the "nawab" of Sardhana in the North-Indian state of Uttar Pradesh.
The nawab title was a hereditary title the family gained thanks to services rendered to the British by an earlier ancestor, Jan-Fishan Khan.
Jan-Fishan Khan was an earlier ancestor of Idries Shah's paternal family whose services to the British earned the family its hereditary title.
